title: Why People Are More Than Problems to Solve
headline: How to See Difficult People as Image-Bearers
headline_sub: People Are More Than Problems to Solve
tagline: Every person carries a story you cannot see and a value you did not create.
seo_title: How to Treat Difficult People: Image-Bearers (Genesis 1:27) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: When we stop seeing image-bearers, we start seeing inconveniences. A devotional for men on Genesis 1:27 and James 3:9 about difficult people.
verse_text: So God created mankind in His own image….

scriptures.text: So God created mankind in His own image….
With the tongue we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings, who have been made in God’s likeness.

blocks.text: One of the quickest ways to drift from the heart of God is to stop seeing people as image-bearers.

items: When people frustrate us….
we label them,
dismiss them,
avoid them,
use them,
judge them,
reduce them.

blocks.text: we stop seeing a person and start seeing a problem.
But every person you encounter, the difficult one, the needy one, the frustrating one, the person who disagrees with you, bears the image of God.

items: The way you see people determines the way you treat people.
And the way you treat people reveals more about your heart than theirs.
Have you ever noticed how often people feel like interruptions?
The coworker who keeps asking questions.
The child who needs attention.
The spouse who wants a conversation.
The stranger moving too slowly.
The person who disagrees with you.
Our flesh naturally asks: “How is this person affecting my agenda?”
God asks: “Can you see this person the way I do?”
Every human being carries dignity because every human being reflects something of their Creator.
Not because they’ve earned it.
Not because they agree with you.
Not because they’re easy to love.
Because God placed His image upon them.
The person who hurt you.
The person who frustrates you.
The person who votes differently.
The person who seems impossible.
All image-bearers.
James points out a startling contradiction.
We praise God…. and then dishonor people made in God’s likeness.
How we treat people matters because of whose image they carry.
Notice how Jesus treated people.
Tax collectors. Fishermen. Children. Widows. Lepers. The blind. The broken. The outcast.
Where others saw problems…. Jesus saw people.
Where others saw labels…. Jesus saw image-bearers.
The more we walk with Jesus…. the more our vision changes.
Surface thought: “This person is my problem.”
Possible root: pride, self-focus, frustration, lack of empathy.
Core lie: “People exist to serve my agenda.”
Truth: People are not interruptions to my mission. Many times they are the mission.
Anyone can love easy people.
The way of Jesus teaches us to see people before problems.
